entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Heart - His understanding is always present with him and ready to direct him. He mentions the right hand, because that is the common instrument of action. A fool's - His understanding is not effectual to govern his affections and actions.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Walketh - In his daily conversation. He saith - He discovers his folly to all that meet him.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The spirit - The passion. Leave not - In anger or discontent. Continue in a diligent and faithful discharge of thy duty, and modestly and humbly submit to him. Yielding - A gentle and submissive carriage.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The rich - Wise and worthy men, rich in endowments of mind.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: An hedge - Whereby another man's fields or vineyards are distinguished, that he may either take away their fruits, or enlarge his own fields.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Whoso removeth - Stones too heavy for them: who rashly attempts things too high and hard for them.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wisdom - As wisdom instructs a man in the smallest matters, so it is useful for a man's direction in all weighty affairs.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Without - If not prevented by the art and care of the charmer; which practice he does not justify, but only mentions by way of resemblance.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Gracious - Procure him favour with those who hear him.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Full of words - Forward to promise and boast what he will do, whereas none can be sure of future events, even during his own life, much more after his death.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wearieth - Fools discover their folly by their wearisome and fruitless endeavours after things which are too high for them. Because - He is ignorant of those things which are most easy, as of the way to the great city whither he is going.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A child - Either in age, or childish qualities. Eat - Give up themselves to eating and drinking. Morning - The fittest time for God's service, for the dispatch of weighty affairs, and for sitting in judgment.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Nobles - Not so much by birth, as by their noble dispositions.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy thought - In the most secret manner. The rich - Princes or governors. A bird - The king will hear of it by unknown and unsuspected hands, as if a bird had heard and carried the report of it.
